abertura: Is evil something that people become or something that they discover in themselves? Rousseau would say that we are born good and that society corrupts us,
transcricao: Is evil something that people become or something that they discover in themselves? Rousseau would say that we are born good and that society corrupts us, whereas Hobbes believed that humans, when left to our own volition, are cruel and nasty creatures. Carl Jung believed that everyone has a shadow and it's not something that's created, it's something that's revealed. Hannah Arendt studied Adolf Eichmann, who was a Nazi official responsible for the deaths of many. She concluded that he was just an ordinary man that followed orders and stopped thinking. The Stanford prison experiment showed us that normal students quickly turn cruel once handed power and a uniform. The reality is most of us have moral luck, a concept that argues most people don't do bad things because they've never been put in a position where it's convenient. You've never stolen, but have you ever been desperate? You've never cheated on your partner, but has anyone else ever actively pursued you? The truth is most of us only act good because we fear the consequences of acting evil. It's the path of least resistance. It is biologically hardwiring us at any given moment to do whatever benefits us the most. So maybe the real question isn't where evil comes from, but what it takes to bring yours out.

abertura: The most valuable thing you own isn't your money, it's your attention. And every time you open your phone, someone is competing for it.
transcricao: The most valuable thing you own isn't your money, it's your attention. And every time you open your phone, someone is competing for it. This device right here makes you forget what you really want. When all you do is consume and you never create, how could you possibly live a fruitful life? But the same screen that's distracting millions of people can also change your life for the better. The question is, are you going to serve your algorithm or is your algorithm going to serve you?

abertura: If you're evil, but admit that you're evil, people will weirdly let it slide. In psychology, they call this preemptive self-disclosure.
transcricao: If you're evil, but admit that you're evil, people will weirdly let it slide. In psychology, they call this preemptive self-disclosure. You're effectively hijacking the insult. Now they can't hold it above you anymore. You're neutralizing the shame. The thing is, most people want to feel superior in some way, so they like to point the finger at you. But the second you take accountability, now they don't have anything over you and they don't know what to do anymore.
